I played through this on Gamepass so disregard my Steam hours. To give you an idea, I'm someone who thinks that almost all roguelites, collectathons, 2d sidescrolling platformers, metroidvanias, and pixel graphics games are TERRIBLE . So, when this was recommended to me I prepared myself for what should have felt like the worst game created by mankind to date. Instead, imagine my shock to discover that this game is an absolute KNOCKOUT on every level you could measure. It bleeds passion and oozes fun in a way that only something created by an extremely talented team with a very clear vision could have made. It's so visually expressive and the gameplay is tight and responsive, with so many easter eggs and secrets that never stopped being enjoyable to find. An utter thrill to complete and absolute must-play.

I am apart of the ~1% who has gotten 100% of achievements in this game, and even I haven't seen all there is to experience. 

Perhaps one of the most competently made video games I have ever experienced, there was never a single second of Dead Cells that I didn't enjoy. It is a testament to the game that the most difficult and unfair enemy is not unfun, and there is truly only one single boss that I dont enjoy. I still to this day load up the boss rush mode just to see if I can still do them all hitless.

The only real slight to this game is that the middle difficulties (specifically level 3-4), can feel a little boring to get through. But in the face of how many hundreds of hours are spent with the gas held all the way down I think this is a small issue. 

I also don't think its a totally unfair critique to talk about how the games best content is very arguably locked behind DLC (specifically, Castlevania and Queen of the Sea, with Fatal Falls having probably my favorite level). But this will depend on your views of DLC and you wallet. Overall I would recommend them without a second thought.

I dont think it has to be said, but the achievements are also excellent. Easily one of the best experiences i have ever had completing a game, they're tough and hard as nails, but NEVER unfair. They force you to perfect your gameplay in ways you would never think to otherwise, and can act as a checklist that nudge you into playing the game as intended. 

I dedicated about four or more years playing dead cells on and off to get 100%, and the game feels just as vast, open ended, and repayable as the first day i started. So, like, play it.

Game is very good, very funny, but past the first 2 boss cells it's really punishing and it takes just small errors or distractions to fuck up even the best runs. genuinely makes rage over stupid shit. the platiforming side of the game is so so so so annoying, there are so so so many times where the beheaded goes where the hell he wants and more often than not that's a reason i take damage. Dodging is either really satisfying or insanely unresponsive, there is no in between. it's absurdely inconsistent for me. all of this is not a major problem when you get to heal often during the first boss cells, but later on it just makes for an excruciating and unfun experience. Most would define this skill issue, but having played 100+ hours over multiple platforms i would at least expect to understand the basics of the game, and yet everytime here i am taking damage in the most bullshit way possible. this game is probably a very enjoyable experience if you are someone who tends to not get angry at all..
All things said, i love this game, but i wish those fucking red flies got deleted from this universe.

Tried this game before it had alot of DLCs and since then still replay this from time to time. A pinnacle in my heart that defined roguelike games.

- My earliest experience of roguelike games that keeps giving more and more, changed my opinion on platformer games "looks too boring" for my taste, turns out its my taste that is the problem.

- Risk management and daring to challenge is always encouraged and nurtured throughout every rounds, and it just revealed to me that venturing into randomness and unknown is not that scary anyways, although I do find this is one of the most challenging roguelike games for me.

- The humor of Headless being unbothered by the chaos and darkness in the world is what keep the loops going. But it may also because Headless don't literally...uhm...die...?

- Elements of surprise from weapons, equipment, enemies and the environment keep revealing from stage to stage, rounds and rounds of loop. A great addition to keep exploring this ever-changing game without feeling repetitive and boring fast.

I would recommend those who think this game is too pixel graphic and 2D for them: Come and find out, you'll find yourself opening the door to a whole new perspective...
